name: satisfaction
description: The momentary sense that a perception meets what was expected but even so, it doesn't significantly effect your world.
perceptions: Something I just perceived is pretty much what I expected.
The results aren't important in the grand scale of things.
examples: Inspecting the results of a job don't reveal any problems.
The spare vacuum is still dead as expected after trying a different electrical outlet.
The remote control is in the right place for once.

comparisons.description: 'Satisfaction' is just a gentle 'checkbox' feeling of confirmation that expectations are met and the results don't really change your overall situation. 'Delight' is when something exceeds your expectations in a positive way, causing you to upgrade your assessment of the situation for the better.

You can feel satisfaction and relief at the same time if the expectation was not clear but the preference was clear. For example, say you're not sure whether you closed the garage door, but find you come home to find it closed. You're probably satisfied with yourself but also a little relieved because you weren't sure.

variations.name: satisfied with yourself
variations.description: The sense that you lived up to your own expectations for something that matters to someone.
perceptions: I lived up to what I expected of myself.
The results are likely to please some of my social or existential contacts.

commentaries.quote: We're always judging whether events and people's behavior meet our expectations. If they just reach that bar, we may feel satisfaction or delight depending on whether the results cause an upgrade in future expectations.

As pattern-making and -matching machines, our brains are constantly testing perceptions against patterns. Satisfaction is the wonderful scenario where the expectation held true against what was perceived.
To be able to look back upon one's past life with satisfaction is to live twice.
Perfectionism rarely begets perfection, or satisfaction - only disappointment.
Happiness does not come from doing easy work but from the afterglow of satisfaction that comes after the achievement of a difficult task that demanded our best.
We always want more. Whether it is better clothes, a bigger house, faster cars, or the latest gadgets, satisfaction in these days of consumerism is difficult to find.

4,3,2,1.description: satisfaction can happen in any of the spheres: physical, social, mental, existential.
